ordered_diagnoses: Myocardial Infarction with Non-Obstructive Coronary Artery Disease

candidates.name: Acute Coronary Syndrome
support_spans: 1 hour of acute, severe precordial chest pain radiating to his left arm
Initial serum troponin I level: 1.159 ng/mL (normal range ≤0.028 ng/mL)
95% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results are consistent with acute coronary syndrome.

candidates.name: ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)
support_spans: 2-mm ST-segment elevation in avR
Reciprocal ST-segment depression in leads II, III, and aVF
candidates.why: The patient's ECG findings are consistent with STEMI.

candidates.name: Non-ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (NSTEMI)
support_spans: Upsloping ST-segment depression leads V1 through V6
Tall, symmetric T waves in leads V2 and V3
candidates.why: The patient's ECG findings are also consistent with NSTEMI.

key_evidence_spans: 1 hour of acute, severe precordial chest pain radiating to his left arm

candidates.name: Variant Angina (Prinzmetal's Angina)
support_spans: acute, severe precordial chest pain radiating to his left arm, accompanied by sweating and nausea
ST-segment elevation in avR
reciprocal ST-segment depression in leads II, III, and aVF
contradict_spans: 95% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and ECG findings are consistent with variant angina, but the presence of significant coronary stenosis suggests a possible overlap with stable angina.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be easily missed due to its rarity and similarity in presentation to other types of angina.

candidates.name: Myocardial Infarction with Non-Obstructive Coronary Artery Disease
support_spans: Initial serum troponin I level: 1.159 ng/mL
Hypomotility in the anterior wall
Left ventricular ejection fraction: 57%
contradict_spans: 95% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery
candidates.why: The patient's elevated troponin level and echocardiography findings suggest myocardial infarction, but the presence of significant coronary stenosis does not entirely explain the extent of cardiac damage.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be underconsidered due to the presence of significant coronary stenosis, which may lead to a focus on obstructive coronary artery disease.
